correctness.rationale: For all \(0<|a|<1\), \(|b|\le1-|a|^2\) gives a bounded quadratic composition by an explicit Gaussian change of variables; coherent kernels and failure of \(T1\) rule out all larger |b|. For strict inequality a Gaussian Bargmann Gram kernel \(K_A\) is derived for \(A=T^*T\), with constants \(h,\alpha,\gamma\). Gaussian exponential generating eigenvectors yield every \(\lambda_0 r^n\); positive trace-class A has trace \(1/\sqrt{(1-|a|^2)^2-|b|^2}\), equal to \(\lambda_0/(1-r)\), so the eigenfamily is complete, including the absence of a missing kernel because T is injective. At equality \(K_A=|a|^{-1}K_{e^{-cP^2}}\), with P the self-adjoint momentum operator; the Fourier multiplier \(e^{-c\xi^2}\) proves pure absolutely continuous modulus spectrum and flat approximation numbers. Exact root expansion proves the sqrt blow-up coefficient. Finite monomial Gram and parameter identities were checked from the packaged Python standard-library script; those checks are not used as infinite-dimensional proofs. The conclusion concerns \(|T|\) at the boundary, not spectral type of nonnormal T.

value.rationale: The natural quadratic exponential Fock weighted-composition family has a genuine compact/noncompact boundary at \(|b|=1-|a|^2\). The exact spectrum of \(|T|\) changes from a fully quantified geometric discrete sequence with every Schatten quasi-norm to a purely absolutely continuous momentum-heat multiplier, and all approximation numbers become flat. The sharp universal \(\varepsilon^{-1/2}\) divergence with its explicit parameter constant quantifies that transition. This complete quantitative phase classification is mathematically motivated beyond previously known qualitative boundedness/compactness or a generic exponential upper bound; it does not claim the underlying Gaussian/Mehler method is new.
